dedupe_keys.name: ofr bank systemic risk monitor bsrm

description: The OFR Bank Systemic Risk Monitor is a collection of key measures for monitoring systemic risks posed by the largest banks, extending the earlier OFR G-SIB Scores Interactive Chart. It includes systemic importance scores for international and U.S. banks calculated by averaging the five categories of the Basel Committee's assessment method for global systemically important banks (size, interconnectedness, substitutability, complexity and cross-jurisdictional activity), with the corresponding capital surcharge buckets, the U.S. G-SIB surcharges under the Federal Reserve method, the OFR Contagion Index, leverage, assets and equity, and short-term wholesale funding. Charts show each bank's score by year and category with indicator values such as total exposures and intra-financial assets and liabilities. Coverage is the largest international and U.S. banks. Chart data and all data sets can be downloaded free of charge; no licence is stated on the page. Caveats: the page notes that regulators may calculate surcharges with a different method, and scores are yearly. For simulation it gives the size and interconnectedness of systemically important banks for financial contagion and network stress scenarios. Related catalogue records include NYU V-Lab SRISK, the OFR Financial Stress Index and GLEIF LEI data.
